solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Give a tick to dramatist in dialogue

indicators.note: dialogue is speech, so the playwright's name is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: Anton Chekhov, the Russian playwright

explanation.surface: Praise a playwright for the lines he gives his characters to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in dialogue' asks for the sound: CHEKHOV said aloud matches CHECK OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: To check off an item on a list is to mark it with a tick as done.

clue.text: Ditches husband, I see, then son

parts.note: 'aha!' is the exclamation of someone who sees the point
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: A husband ditches his wife, realisation dawns, then the son leaves too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ha-ha is a sunken ditch with a wall, used as a hidden boundary in landscaped gardens.

clue.text: Suck up large leaves having a spicy, Indian taste

indicators.note: the large item departs, so that letter is taken out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the flavour of a curry, the spiced Indian dish
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone inhales big leaves seasoned with hot Indian spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a verb: L (large) leaves CURRY FLAVOUR, leaving CURRY FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To curry favour is to flatter someone in the hope of advantage, which is sucking up.

clue.text: Provide bananas round area given too much bread

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Supply bananas around the place, handing out too much bread as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' is the anagram signal working on PROVIDE plus A.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, so someone given too much of it has been overpaid.

clue.text: Polish is the main subject learnt here?

definitions.text: Polish is the main subject learnt here?

parts.words: Polish is the main subject learnt here?
parts.note: read as polish, social refinement, this is the school that teaches it; a language school for Polish is the false reading

explanation.surface: A question about a school where the Polish language dominates the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P suggests the language; the polish meant is refinement and social graces, the final touch to a young person's education.
explanation.definitionFit: A finishing school teaches young women etiquette and social graces, giving them polish.

clue.text: A head of militia's back with gun

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, here taken from the end of militia

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A militia leader returns armed with a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'militia's back' is the A at the end of militia; 'A head' is the definition, meaning per person.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means for each one, the same as a head when sharing out costs or items.

clue.text: A fee, we hear, for what solicitors do

indicators.note: we are told to listen, so the words are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: a fee is a cost, so 'a cost'

explanation.surface: A fee, so rumour has it, for whatever a lawyer does.
explanation.walkthrough: The solicitors are not lawyers but people who solicit, approaching strangers in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to approach someone and make an offer, which is to accost them.

clue.text: Wicked eminence needing no introduction

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, which is dropped

parts.note: an eminence is a hill, a piece of high ground

explanation.surface: A wicked figure so prominent they need no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill can mean evil or bad, as in ill deeds or ill will, so it means wicked.

clue.text: Business hides account, along with fraudulent racket

indicators.note: the company conceals the account within itself

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
phony means fake or fraudulent

explanation.surface: A firm conceals an account as part of a fraudulent scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scheme, matching the surface, but it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, and cacophony is a harsh mixture of sounds.

clue.text: Rogue has to trap soldiers by East Riding

indicators.note: the rearranged letters catch the soldiers inside them
a rogue goes astray, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A rogue has trapped soldiers near the East Riding of Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: AHS (the anagram of HAS, from 'Rogue') holds OR. The East Riding is a district of Yorkshire, but 'Riding' here means on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahorse is an old word for on horseback, the state of a person riding.

clue.text: Jewellery put away quickly along with pretty fabric

parts.note: to neck food or drink is British slang for swallowing it fast
lace is a delicate decorative fabric

explanation.surface: Jewellery is hastily stowed away along with some pretty fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for downing a drink fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace is an item of jewellery worn around the neck.

clue.text: Before retiring, American is looking grey

indicators.note: the American comes first, ahead of the retiring part

parts.note: a retiring person is shy and reserved

explanation.surface: An American looks grey and drawn shortly before retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving work but means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means ash-coloured, a pale grey, as of a sickly complexion.

clue.text: Final message about boring job with trips abroad

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about drills into the rearranged letters
abroad means all over the place, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A last note about a dull job that involves travelling overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' means drilling through: C goes inside SRIPT (the anagram of TRIPS, from 'abroad'), making SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A postscript is a message added at the very end of a letter.

clue.text: Shake and wave a smashing bit of machinery

parts.note: to rock something is to shake it
a breaker is a wave that breaks on the shore

explanation.surface: Shake things up and wave goodbye to a great piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' seems to mean excellent, but the machine literally smashes stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock breaker is a machine used in quarrying and mining to smash large stones.

clue.text: Musical 24, one who doesn't believe in Buccaneer

parts.note: a pagan is someone outside the main religions, a non-believer
Buccaneer is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A musical genius who has no faith in Buccaneer the setter.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is VIRTUOSO, so the definition reads 'musical virtuoso'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian violinist, the archetypal musical virtuoso.

clue.text: Flavour enhancer, Charlie's admitted, is like a drug

indicators.note: is admitted means let in, so the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: an additive is something added to food, such as a flavour enhancer
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie confesses that the flavour enhancer is as habit-forming as a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie's admitted' reads as a confession but means Charlie is let inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something addictive creates dependence, just as narcotics do.

clue.text: Conservative bound to get axe

parts.note: to bound is to leap or hop

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is certain to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' suggests certainty, but bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to cut it, which is to chop it.

clue.text: Old solver's in teams playing in purple

indicators.note: the old word sits within the reordered letters
the teams are in play, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: thy is the old word for your, and the clue speaks to the solver as you

explanation.surface: An ageing solver lines up with teams playing in a purple strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the old possessive inside AMEST, the anagram from 'playing'. The clue addresses the solver as you, so the solver's is your, in old form thy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz, and the word names that colour.

clue.text: Edible tuber filled double sandwiches

indicators.note: the words close round the answer like slices of bread around a filling

explanation.surface: An edible root vegetable packed into double-decker sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'filLED DOuble'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddo is the starchy edible root of the taro plant, a type of tuber.

clue.text: Consoles limping children

parts.note: game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg
boys are male children

explanation.surface: Someone comforts children who are limping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consoles' looks like a verb meaning comforts; it is the noun for gaming devices.
explanation.definitionFit: The Game Boy is Nintendo's handheld video game console.

clue.text: Radio broadcast with time for expert

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A radio show that makes time for an expert guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, giving ADROI; 'with' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful and clever, the quality of someone expert.

clue.text: Cross between a chicken and a cheetah?

definitions.text: Cross between a chicken and a cheetah?

parts.words: Cross between a chicken and a cheetah?
parts.note: a cowardly person (chicken) combined with a big cat gives a timid cat

explanation.surface: An odd hybrid animal, half chicken and half cheetah.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken is slang for a coward, and the cheetah supplies the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaredy-cat is a childish term for a timid, fearful person.

clue.text: Horny creatures seen regularly in bed like so

indicators.note: every other letter of the following words is picked out, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Randy creatures spotted often in bed doing it this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of 'bEd LiKe So'. Horny means bearing horns, which elks have as antlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Elks are large deer whose males carry antlers, so they are horned animals.

clue.text: Death toll?

parts.note: not a count of fatalities but the bell tolled for a death

explanation.surface: A query about how many people died.
explanation.walkthrough: A death toll is normally a casualty figure; here it is a bell literally tolling for a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the solemn ringing of a bell to announce a death or funeral.

clue.text: Wizard with a lot of goodness and love, really!

indicators.note: most of the word is taken, losing its final letter

parts.note: virtue is moral goodness
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
'so' is used for emphasis, as in 'it is so!', meaning really

explanation.surface: An admiring cry about a wizard brimming with goodness and love.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard can be a person of outstanding skill, and a virtuoso is a brilliant performer.

clue.text: Drink milk from here, mostly

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: milk comes from a teat

explanation.surface: Drink the milk that comes mostly from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a common hot beverage, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Did rabbit fly after Tibetan cattle?

indicators.note: the fly comes after the cattle in the answer

parts.note: yaks are long-haired cattle of Tibet
a ked is a wingless parasitic fly found on sheep

explanation.surface: Did a rabbit flee from chasing Tibetan oxen?
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering, as is to yak.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit and yak are both slang verbs for talking at length, so yakked means rabbited.

clue.text: Geordie entertainers getting transfer

parts.note: Dec (Declan Donnelly) is one half of the Newcastle TV duo Ant and Dec; Geordie means from Newcastle
Ant (Anthony McPartlin) is the other half of the entertaining duo

explanation.surface: Two comedians from Newcastle are moving to another network.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase names Ant and Dec, a British TV presenting duo from Newcastle upon Tyne, taken here in the order Dec then Ant.
explanation.definitionFit: To decant is to pour liquid from one vessel into another, so to transfer it.

clue.text: Textual errors I found in stellar novel

indicators.note: the letter I is placed within the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer spots typing errors in a brilliant novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal: I goes inside LTERALS (the anagram of STELLAR).
explanation.definitionFit: Literals are printers' misprints, typographical errors in a text.
